title: Thunder finalizing trade of Aaron Wiggins to Hawks for two second-round picks: Sources
author: Joel Lorenzi
content:
The Oklahoma City Thunder are trading guard Aaron Wiggins to the Atlanta Hawks for two future second-round picks, sources confirmed to The Athletic on Sunday.

The Thunder will receive Atlanta’s 2030 second-round pick, as well as the least favorable of the Hawks/Lakers second-round pick in 2032. They also clear a roster spot while simultaneously shedding salary as they juggle several players — namely Lu Dort and Isaiah Hartenstein — with approaching team options. The trade leaves the Thunder with 14 players under contract. They will enter the first round of the NBA Draft on Tuesday with two selections and can reduce their projected luxury tax penalty.

Drafted with the 55th pick in the 2021 NBA Draft, Wiggins was among the Thunder’s premier development stories. The Maryland product emerged from OKC’s rebuilding seasons to become a legitimate bench scoring threat, averaging a career-high 12 points during the Thunder’s title-winning 2024-25 season.

Wiggins’ minutes dwindled with the progression of several of the Thunder’s younger guards. Between both the Western Conference semifinals and the West finals, Wiggins averaged just 4.5 minutes. He gives Atlanta, which pivoted last season with its trade of Trae Young, some firepower on its bench.

Wiggins is set to make just over $9 million next season on a declining contract with three years remaining, including a team option in the final year of the deal at just 4.49 percent of the projected cap during the 2028-29 season.

Atlanta holds an $11 million trade exception created by its February trade of Luke Kennard. The deal likely won’t become official until July 6, when the NBA’s free-agency moratorium period ends. The Hawks still possess some flexibility, with decisions on Buddy Hield (partially guaranteed) and Jonathan Kuminga (team option) pending.

Taking in Wiggins without sending out any salary likely terminates any notion of the Hawks operating as a cap-room team this summer. Instead, they will take Wiggins into the $11 million traded-player exception created last February with the Kennard deal. The addition of Wiggins as yet another offense-oriented wing off the bench also makes one question the futures of Buddy Hield (partially guaranteed) and Jonathan Kuminga (team option), whose fates will be decided in the next few days.
